course: AP Biology - Molecules, Cells, Heredity and Ecology
attribution: Original scope and sequence authored for the Luminfest Learning Harness, dedicated to the public domain under CC0.
scope: Structure only: concept titles, unit order and prerequisite intent. No third-party curriculum text is reproduced, and no restricted source is ingested.
description: The AP Biology course framework: the chemistry of life, cell structure and function, cellular energetics, cell communication and the cell cycle, heredity, gene expression and regulation, natural selection, and ecology.

topics.topic: The chemistry that life is built from

concepts.title: Structure of water and hydrogen bonding
concepts.summary: Hydrogen bonding gives water cohesion, adhesion, a high specific heat and solvent power, which is why life depends on it.

concepts.title: Elements of life
concepts.summary: Carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, phosphorus and sulfur build the molecules of life.
prerequisites: Structure of water and hydrogen bonding

concepts.title: Biological macromolecules: carbohydrates
concepts.summary: Simple sugars join into polysaccharides that serve as fuel or as structural material.

concepts.title: Biological macromolecules: lipids
concepts.summary: Fats store energy densely while phospholipids build the membranes that compartmentalise cells.

concepts.title: Biological macromolecules: proteins
concepts.summary: A protein folds into a shape determined by its amino acid sequence, and the shape determines its function.

concepts.title: Biological macromolecules: nucleic acids
concepts.summary: DNA stores information in a stable double strand while RNA carries and interprets it.

concepts.title: Enzymes as biological catalysts
concepts.summary: Enzymes lower activation energy and are unchanged by the reaction they speed up.

concepts.title: Enzyme structure and the active site
concepts.summary: A substrate binds a specific active site, and the induced fit grips it more tightly.

concepts.title: Factors affecting enzyme activity
concepts.summary: Temperature, pH and substrate concentration change rate, and beyond the optimum the enzyme denatures.
prerequisites: Enzyme structure and the active site

concepts.title: Enzyme inhibition and regulation
concepts.summary: Competitive and non-competitive inhibitors slow a reaction, and allosteric regulation tunes it.

concepts.title: pH, buffers and cellular conditions
concepts.summary: Buffers resist pH change, which keeps enzyme shape and function stable.

concepts.title: Cell structure: prokaryotic and eukaryotic
concepts.summary: Prokaryotes lack membrane-bound organelles, which is the deepest structural divide among cells.

concepts.title: Organelles and compartmentalisation
concepts.summary: Each organelle specialises in one job, and a cell can do only what its organelles allow.

concepts.title: Endosymbiosis
concepts.summary: Mitochondria and chloroplasts descend from engulfed bacteria, which explains their own DNA and double membrane.

concepts.title: Cell size and surface area to volume ratio
concepts.summary: As a cell grows its surface area to volume ratio falls, which limits how large it can be.

concepts.title: Cell specialisation and differentiation
concepts.summary: Every cell of an organism shares the same DNA, so differentiation is about which genes are expressed.
prerequisites: Cell size and surface area to volume ratio

concepts.title: Microscopy and the study of cells
concepts.summary: Magnification and resolution are different limits, and resolution is what actually restricts detail.

concepts.title: Cell membrane structure
concepts.summary: The fluid mosaic model explains selective permeability as proteins embedded in a moving lipid bilayer.

concepts.title: Passive transport and diffusion
concepts.summary: Net movement down a gradient needs no energy, and its rate depends on the gradient, distance and temperature.

concepts.title: Osmosis and water potential
concepts.summary: Water moves toward lower water potential, which is why cells shrink or burst in different solutions.

concepts.title: Facilitated diffusion and channel proteins
concepts.summary: Polar and charged solutes cross through specific proteins down their gradient, with no energy cost.

concepts.title: Active transport
concepts.summary: Moving a substance against its gradient costs energy, which is why it stops when respiration stops.

concepts.title: Bulk transport: endocytosis and exocytosis
concepts.summary: Vesicles move large particles in and out, which is how a cell moves material the membrane cannot pass.

concepts.title: Energy, metabolism and free energy
concepts.summary: Free-energy change decides whether a reaction can proceed spontaneously.

concepts.title: ATP and energy coupling
concepts.summary: ATP transfers a phosphate group, coupling an energy-releasing reaction to one that needs energy.

concepts.title: Coupled reactions and metabolic pathways
concepts.summary: Metabolism is a set of enzyme-catalysed steps, each coupled to the next.

concepts.title: Glycolysis
concepts.summary: Glucose splits into pyruvate with a small net gain of ATP and reduced electron carriers.

concepts.title: The Krebs cycle
concepts.summary: Acetyl-CoA is oxidised completely, releasing carbon dioxide and loading electron carriers.

concepts.title: Oxidative phosphorylation and the electron transport chain
concepts.summary: Electron transport pumps protons, and the resulting gradient drives ATP synthase.

concepts.title: Fermentation
concepts.summary: Without oxygen, cells regenerate the electron carrier using an organic molecule and gain far less ATP.

concepts.title: Photosynthesis: light-dependent reactions
concepts.summary: Light energy splits water, releasing oxygen and producing ATP and reduced carriers.
prerequisites: Oxidative phosphorylation and the electron transport chain

concepts.title: Photosynthesis: the Calvin cycle
concepts.summary: ATP and reduced carriers fix carbon dioxide into sugar using the enzyme rubisco.

concepts.title: Factors affecting photosynthesis and respiration
concepts.summary: Light intensity, carbon dioxide, temperature and oxygen availability each limit the rate.

concepts.title: Signal transduction pathways
concepts.summary: A signal is received, transduced through a cascade and converted into a cellular response.

concepts.title: Receptors and ligands
concepts.summary: A ligand binds a specific receptor, and the receptor type decides whether the cell changes fast or slowly.

concepts.title: Signal amplification and second messengers
concepts.summary: A cascade multiplies the signal so a few molecules produce a large response.

concepts.title: Feedback and homeostasis
concepts.summary: Negative feedback opposes a change while positive feedback amplifies it.

concepts.title: The cell cycle and its regulation
concepts.summary: Growth, synthesis and division are ordered phases policed by checkpoints.

concepts.title: Mitosis
concepts.summary: Mitosis produces genetically identical cells for growth and repair.
prerequisites: The cell cycle and its regulation

concepts.title: Checkpoints and cancer
concepts.summary: Failure of cell-cycle control lets damaged cells divide unchecked.

concepts.title: Apoptosis
concepts.summary: Programmed cell death removes damaged or unneeded cells as a normal part of development.

concepts.title: Meiosis
concepts.summary: Meiosis halves the chromosome number and reshuffles genes, creating genetic variation.

concepts.title: Genetic variation in meiosis
concepts.summary: Independent assortment and crossing over make each gamete genetically distinct.

concepts.title: Mendelian inheritance
concepts.summary: Alleles segregate and assort independently, which predicts the ratios of offspring phenotypes.

concepts.title: Monohybrid and dihybrid crosses
concepts.summary: Punnett squares predict offspring ratios from parental genotypes.

concepts.title: Probability in genetics
concepts.summary: Inheritance follows probability rules, so larger samples approach predicted ratios.

concepts.title: Non-Mendelian inheritance
concepts.summary: Incomplete dominance, codominance and multiple alleles produce phenotypes that simple dominance cannot explain.

concepts.title: Sex-linked inheritance
concepts.summary: Genes on the sex chromosomes produce different inheritance patterns in males and females.

concepts.title: Pedigrees and inheritance analysis
concepts.summary: A pedigree traces a trait through a family and can reveal its mode of inheritance.

concepts.title: Chromosomal inheritance
concepts.summary: Genes are carried on chromosomes, so chromosome behaviour explains inheritance patterns.

concepts.title: Linked genes and recombination
concepts.summary: Genes close together on a chromosome tend to be inherited together, and recombination frequency measures distance.

concepts.title: Environmental effects on phenotype
concepts.summary: The phenotype is the product of genotype and environment, so identical genotypes can differ.

concepts.title: DNA structure and replication
concepts.summary: Complementary base pairing allows semi-conservative replication with proofreading.

concepts.title: Transcription
concepts.summary: RNA polymerase makes an RNA copy of a gene, which is the first step of expression.

concepts.title: RNA processing
concepts.summary: Eukaryotic RNA is capped, spliced and tailed before it leaves the nucleus.

concepts.title: Translation
concepts.summary: Ribosomes read codons and assemble amino acids into a polypeptide.

concepts.title: The genetic code
concepts.summary: Codons are redundant but unambiguous, which limits the effect of some mutations.

concepts.title: Gene regulation in prokaryotes
concepts.summary: Operons let bacteria switch whole pathways on and off in response to the environment.

concepts.title: Gene regulation in eukaryotes
concepts.summary: Eukaryotes regulate at transcription, RNA processing, translation and after translation.

concepts.title: Mutations
concepts.summary: Substitutions, insertions and deletions change protein sequence, and frameshifts are usually more damaging.

concepts.title: Biotechnology and genetic engineering
concepts.summary: Restriction enzymes, PCR, gel electrophoresis and sequencing let genes be read and manipulated.

concepts.title: Genome evolution
concepts.summary: Genomes change through duplication, rearrangement and horizontal transfer over long timescales.

concepts.title: Natural selection and adaptation
concepts.summary: Heritable variation plus differential reproduction changes trait frequencies across generations.

concepts.title: Evidence for evolution
concepts.summary: Fossils, biogeography, comparative anatomy and molecular data converge on common descent.

concepts.title: Artificial selection
concepts.summary: Selective breeding shows how quickly allele frequencies shift under strong selection.

concepts.title: Population genetics and allele frequencies
concepts.summary: Evolution is a change in allele frequency in a population over time.

concepts.title: Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium
concepts.summary: The null model predicts constant allele frequencies when no evolutionary force acts.

concepts.title: Genetic drift and gene flow
concepts.summary: Chance and migration change allele frequencies without any fitness advantage.

concepts.title: Speciation
concepts.summary: Reproductive isolation, often after geographic separation, produces new species.

concepts.title: Phylogeny and classification
concepts.summary: Shared derived characters build a tree of relationships among lineages.

concepts.title: Extinction and biodiversity
concepts.summary: Background and mass extinctions shape the diversity of life, and current rates are unusually high.

concepts.title: Population ecology
concepts.summary: Population size is set by births, deaths, immigration and emigration, and by density-dependent limits.

concepts.title: Population growth models
concepts.summary: Exponential growth assumes unlimited resources while logistic growth approaches a carrying capacity.

concepts.title: Species interactions
concepts.summary: Competition, predation, mutualism and parasitism each change the fitness of the interacting species.

concepts.title: Community ecology
concepts.summary: Species diversity and structure emerge from interactions and disturbance regimes.

concepts.title: Energy flow and trophic levels
concepts.summary: Energy transfer between trophic levels is inefficient, which limits food chain length.

concepts.title: Biogeochemical cycles
concepts.summary: Carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus and water cycle between organisms and the environment.

concepts.title: Ecosystem dynamics and succession
concepts.summary: Disturbance drives succession, and ecosystems differ in how quickly they recover.

concepts.title: Biodiversity and conservation
concepts.summary: Biodiversity has genetic, species and ecosystem components, each with its own threats.

concepts.title: Human impact on ecosystems
concepts.summary: Habitat loss, climate change, pollution and invasive species are the main drivers of biodiversity loss.

concepts.title: Behavioural ecology
concepts.summary: Foraging, mating and social behaviour can be analysed by their effect on fitness.
